varieties.name: Dolgo
varieties.summary: Very tart and juicy with a clean, bright fruitiness; just about pleasant raw when fully ripe but really a kitchen crab. It gives a clear, deep ruby jelly that sets well and a vividly coloured juice.

varieties.name: Dorsett Golden
varieties.summary: Sweet and fairly mild with a Golden Delicious character; lightly crisp and juicy. Flavour is said to be best on fruit ripened in light shade, and it softens quickly after picking.

varieties.name: Duchess of Bedford
varieties.summary: Soft, fine-textured pale flesh with a mild, gently acidic flavour; one reference notes an aniseed note, a trait associated with its Cellini parent. Eat it fresh, as it softens quickly.

varieties.name: Duchess of Oldenburg
varieties.summary: Juicy, rather coarse white flesh with brisk, sharp acidity and only modest sweetness. At its best as an early cooker, collapsing quickly to a tangy, orange-tinted puree; eaten raw it is refreshing but turns mealy within days.

varieties.name: Duchess's Favourite
varieties.summary: Crisp to tender, juicy flesh with a brisk, fairly sharp but not harsh flavour; pleasant straight from the tree though less rich than later apples.

varieties.name: Duck's Bill
varieties.summary: Firm, crisp white flesh that is sweet and rather chewy; no detailed tasting notes have been published.

varieties.name: Duke of Devonshire
varieties.summary: Firm, fine-grained and rather dry flesh with a rich, nutty flavour that balances sweetness against a fruity sharpness, in the same style as Ashmead's Kernel rather than the softer Egremont Russet. It needs a long time in store and is at its best in late winter.

varieties.name: Dumelow's Seedling
varieties.summary: Very firm, crisp, juicy white flesh that is intensely acid. Cooks down to a stiff, pale, strongly flavoured purée, ideal for mincemeat and sauces.

varieties.name: Dunn's Favourite
varieties.summary: No verified tasting notes are available for this name.

varieties.name: Early Harvest
varieties.summary: Tender, crisp, juicy white flesh with a brisk, tangy sub-acid flavour. Best for sauce and pies, and pleasant raw when fully ripe; it goes soft and mealy quickly.

varieties.name: Early Victoria
varieties.summary: Crisp, very acid greenish flesh that softens quickly once ripe; cooks rapidly to a light, frothy, sharp purée.

varieties.name: Easter Orange
varieties.summary: Crisp, firm cream flesh with a sweet, aromatic flavour that develops in store; a late keeper for winter and early spring eating.

varieties.name: Ecklinville
varieties.summary: Fine-grained, tender white flesh with a very sharp, brisk acidity. Cooks quickly to a smooth froth.

varieties.name: Edward VII
varieties.summary: Firm, rather coarse, fairly juicy white flesh with a brisk acidity; an excellent late cooker that makes a well-flavoured purée.

varieties.name: Egremont Russet
varieties.summary: Dense, firm, fairly dry cream flesh with a sweet, distinctly nutty flavour and modest acidity. Crisp at picking, it mellows and becomes richer in store but shrivels if kept too long.

varieties.name: Ein Shemer
varieties.summary: Crisp and juicy, on the sharp side with only moderate sweetness; a pleasant early apple rather than a rich one, and it keeps for only a short time.

varieties.name: Ellison's Orange
varieties.summary: Soft, very juicy yellow flesh, sweet and perfumed, with an unmistakable aniseed note that strengthens a few days after picking. Low in acid; it does not stay at its best for long.

varieties.name: Elstar
varieties.summary: Crisp, juicy cream flesh with an intense, lively sweet-sharp balance and honeyed, aromatic notes. Best quite soon after picking; keeps its sharpness well for cooking.

varieties.name: Elton Beauty
varieties.summary: Soft, fine and very juicy flesh with a lively, fairly sharp and aromatic flavour; best eaten fresh as it does not keep.

varieties.name: Emperor Alexander
varieties.summary: Coarse, rather dry and fairly acid flesh with little aroma; more impressive for size than flavour when raw, but useful for cooking.

varieties.name: Empire
varieties.summary: Crisp, juicy, very white flesh with a sweet flavour and a gentle vinous tang from McIntosh, but less acidity. Best fresh from the tree; resists bruising.

varieties.name: Enterprise
varieties.summary: Firm, crisp cream flesh, moderately juicy, with a sharp, slightly spicy flavour at picking that mellows and improves after a month or two in store. Holds up well in cooking.

varieties.name: Envy
varieties.summary: Very sweet with low acidity and a faint floral note; crisp, juicy, pale flesh that browns very slowly once cut. Firmness holds well in storage.

varieties.name: Esopus Spitzenburg
varieties.summary: Crisp, firm yellow flesh, not especially juicy, with a rich, sweet-sharp, spicy and aromatic flavour that deepens after a few weeks in store. Also excellent for pies.

varieties.name: Evereste
varieties.summary: Grown above all for show; the fruit is sharp and not an eating apple, but it is used alone or with other fruit to make crab apple jelly, where its pectin helps the set.

varieties.name: Fall Pippin
varieties.summary: Tender, juicy, aromatic white flesh tinged yellow, with a rich sweet-sharp balance. Used both raw and for cooking, drying and sauce.

varieties.name: Falstaff
varieties.summary: Crisp, juicy flesh with a fresh sweet-sharp flavour that owes more to James Grieve than to Golden Delicious. Makes good juice.

varieties.name: Fiesta
varieties.summary: Crisp, very juicy cream flesh with a sweet, aromatic Cox-like flavour, easier and crunchier than its parent. Stays firm for months in store, though the aroma and sweetness gradually fade.

varieties.name: Filippa
varieties.summary: A sweet-sharp Calville-type apple eaten fresh and pressed for juice and cider; the juice is pale and not very sweet, so it is often blended.

varieties.name: Flanders Cox
varieties.summary: No reliable tasting notes found for this name.

varieties.name: Fortune
varieties.summary: Fairly firm, slightly coarse, juicy cream flesh with a sweet, aromatic flavour that hints at its Cox parent; best eaten fresh in early autumn.

varieties.name: Francis
varieties.summary: Firm, fine, crisp flesh with a very sweet and aromatic flavour in the Cox tradition.

varieties.name: Freedom
varieties.summary: Crisp, very juicy cream flesh with a mild, sweet-sharp flavour; pleasant rather than intense. Good for sauce, juice and cider blends as well as eating.

varieties.name: Freiherr von Berlepsch
varieties.summary: Intensely flavoured: very juicy, firm, pale-yellow flesh with lively acidity balanced by plenty of sugar and a rich, aromatic finish. Keeps its quality for months in store.

varieties.name: Freyberg
varieties.summary: Fine-textured, juicy, firm cream flesh with a sweet, intense flavour often described as having an aniseed or fennel note on top of a honeyed Golden Delicious base. Sharper and more complex than Golden Delicious, but without the full richness of Cox.

varieties.name: Frostbite
varieties.summary: Intensely sweet and dense, with hard, crunchy, juicy flesh and a deep flavour often likened to molasses or cane sugar. Acidity is low, but the taste is anything but plain; it also makes a rich sweet cider.

varieties.name: Fuji
varieties.summary: Very dense, crisp and juicy flesh with high sugar and low acidity, giving a sweet, honeyed flavour; well-ripened fruit may show glassy watercore that tastes especially sweet. Keeps its texture for months.

varieties.name: Gala
varieties.summary: Crisp, fine, juicy cream flesh with a sweet, low-acid flavour and a light pear-like fragrance. Pleasant and easy rather than complex, and loses crispness after a couple of months.

varieties.name: Gascoyne's Scarlet
varieties.summary: Firm, fine-grained, rather dry white flesh, sweet with only a light, faintly perfumed flavour; sharper at picking and mellower after storage. Grown more for looks, cooking and coloured juice than for depth of flavour.

varieties.name: Gavin
varieties.summary: Crisp, fairly juicy flesh with a delicate, mildly aromatic balance of sweetness and acidity. Pleasant fresh but goes past its best within a few weeks.

varieties.name: George Cave
varieties.summary: Fine-textured, juicy white flesh with a pleasant, lightly acid and gently aromatic flavour, brisker than most other August apples. Softens and goes mealy within days, so eat it straight from the tree.

varieties.name: Gladstone
varieties.summary: Crisp and juicy when just picked, with a sweet, pleasantly aromatic flavour, but it turns soft and slightly floury within a few days.

varieties.name: Glockenapfel
varieties.summary: Dense, firm, almost pure-white flesh with a pronounced, bracing acidity and a fresh aromatic quality that builds after a couple of months in store. Holds its shape in baking; eaten raw it is best in late winter and spring when the sharpness has eased.

varieties.name: Gloster
varieties.summary: Firm, crisp and juicy greenish-cream flesh with a fairly sharp, plain flavour and modest aroma; tarter than the Delicious side of its parentage. Keeps its crunch for months and mellows slightly in store.

varieties.name: Golden Bounty
varieties.summary: Firm, fine, crisp flesh with a rich, brisk, sharply aromatic flavour that recalls an early-season Cox with extra acidity.
